newsitem.title: USA: Williams reorganizes to form energy group.
newsitem.headline: Williams reorganizes to form energy group.

text.p: Williams Cos Inc said Monday it is reporganizing its unregulated energy businesses to more aggressively compete for a larger share of a rapidly evolving energy market.
A new, full-serve energy company, Williams Energy Group, will be the result when the new structure is effective October 1, the company said.

It will combine Williams Field Services Group, Williams Pipe Line Co, Williams Energy Ventures and Williams Energy Services Co, with certain assets and activities remaining segregated for regulatory and financial reasons.
In addition to the new group, Williams Cos operations include its Interstate Pipeline Group with five interstate pipelines and its Communications Technology operations.

Chief executive Keith Bailey said "The fact that we're accomplishing this through an internal merger -- without the costs or organizational turmoil involved when companies with disparate cultures and organizations come together -- is a distinct advantage for our business and our customers.
"Within Williams, this change is evolutionary, not revolutionary," he said.
The company said Steve Cropper will serve as Williams Energy Group's president and chief executive office.

Cropper previously served in that role for Williams Pipe Line, Williams Energy Ventures and Williams Energy Services. As previously announced, he was to assume leadership of Williams Field Services on October 1, succeeding Lloyd Hightower, who is retiring.
"With a span of business stretching from the wellhead to retail marketing and from natural gas to electric power, Williams Energy Group is a full-service station for energy," Cropper said.

In the first six months of 1996, Williams Field Services, Williams Pipe Line, Williams Energy Ventures and Williams Energy Services reported results that when combined total $167 million of operating profit on revenues of $679.7 million. Williams Energy Group's operations will be organized into five divisions -- Enterprise Planning & Business Development, Field Services, Merchant Services, Exploration & Production and Petroleum Services.
Field Services encompasses a sizable portion of Williams Field Services Group's operations, including natural gas gathering and processing, and cogeneration.
Merchant Services assumes the bulk of Williams Energy Services' operations, including natural gas and power marketing and trading.
Petroleum Services encompasses many of the Williams Pipe Line and Williams Energy Ventures operations, including petroleum liquids pipeline transportation, terminal services and ethanol production.
Exploration & Production assumes operations formerly coordinated under Williams Production Company, a unit of Williams Field Services Group.

Enterprise Planning & Business Development will formulate and develop the new company's overall strategies. Mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures and creation of new business fall under the realm of this division.
The Finance and Administration division will be responsible for accounting, information systems, human resources and administrative services for Williams Energy.
